title: Provable unlearning in topic modeling and downstream tasks
subcategory: theory: machine unlearning for anchor-word topic models
task: Provably removing training documents from topic models and fine-tuned heads
problem: Unlearning guarantees exist mainly for supervised learning, not for the pre-train/fine-tune paradigm.
architecture: Anchor-word (spectral) topic model learned from word co-occurrences; unlearning by updating co-occurrence statistics and a projected Newton step on topic recovery plus a Gaussian mechanism for indistinguishability; second algorithm unlearns from a linear head fine-tuned on topics without modifying the base model.
key_results: Unlearning cost is independent of the original dataset size (e.g. projected Newton step O(nr^2) vs recovering topics from anchors when retraining).
After fine-tuning, a larger number of documents can be unlearned without changing the base model; simpler downstream tasks allow more deletions.
strengths: First provable unlearning guarantees in a pre-training/fine-tuning setting, using topic models as a tractable model.

limitations.text: Topic models cannot capture features of modern autoregressive language models; uses traditional differential-privacy-style unlearning definitions.
No empirical experiments on real corpora.
